extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutional administrators preparing NIH R01 (PA-16-160) grant applications (resubmissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH Research Project Grant (Parent R01) resubmission (PA-16-160 style) including required forms, attachments, biosketches, and institutional/resource descriptions. The document is a sample/resubmission application demonstrating expected content and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity (FOA) instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) required submission fields and submission type
rubrics_metrics.description: The SF 424 (R&R) form must be completed, indicating TYPE OF SUBMISSION (Pre-application, Application, Changed/Corrected Application) and TYPE OF APPLICATION (New, Resubmission, Continuation, Renewal, Revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide applicant organization information, contact PD/PI information, DUNS, EIN/TIN, and indicate whether the application is being submitted to other agencies. Ensure the correct boxes (e.g., 'Application', 'Resubmission') are checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accurate applicant and organizational identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant information must include legal name, department/division, street address, city/state/country/ZIP, Organizational DUNS, and contact person for matters involving the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include person to be contacted (name, position/title, phone, email), and the Authorized Representative (name, title, organization, signature and date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and assurances; signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the signatory certifies to the statements contained in the list of certifications and provides required assurances, agreeing to comply with any resulting terms if an award is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature acknowledges the truthfulness of statements and warns that false statements may subject individuals to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). The list of certifications/assurances is contained in the announcement or agency-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project start and end dates; congressional district
rubrics_metrics.description: SF424 requires PROPOSED PROJECT start and ending dates and the CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICTS OF APPLICANT and project/performance site(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter accurate start/end dates (e.g., 04/01/2017 to 03/31/2022) and congressional district codes for applicant and performance sites (e.g., NJ-012, NY-012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments — Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A Project Summary/Abstract attachment is required and must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the Project Summary/Abstract as a separate file (e.g., abstract-resubmission.pdf). The summary should concisely state the aims, significance, and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments — Project Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A Project Narrative attachment is required and must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the Project Narrative (e.g., Narrative-resubmission.pdf) describing public health relevance in plain language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments — Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: A Bibliography & References Cited attachment is required and must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a complete reference list (e.g., bibliography_Staph_resubmission.pdf) supporting the proposal and biosketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments — Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A Facilities & Other Resources attachment is required to describe the institutional environment supporting the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe laboratory, clinical, animal, computer, office, and other resources; list core facilities, available equipment, shared resources, and administrative support (examples given: Frick Laboratory, genomics center, proteomics mass spectrometry center, macromolecular crystallography facility, biological imaging center, Lewis Library).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments — Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: An Equipment attachment must list major equipment available to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List major instruments and capabilities (examples in the sample: MicroTOF-Q II mass spectrometer, Liberty peptide synthesizer, analytical and preparative HPLCs, AKTA FPLC systems with MALS detector, CO2 incubators, microscopes, plate readers, MicroBeta2 scintillation counter, NMR spectrometers, Orbitrap, etc.). Describe how equipment supports the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects involvement questions and follow-up documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must state whether human subjects are involved and, if yes, provide IRB/exemption information and approval status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If YES to human subjects: indicate whether project is exempt, check appropriate exemption numbers, indicate if IRB review is pending or approval date, and provide Human Subject Assurance Number as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals involvement and IACUC review
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must state whether vertebrate animals are used and, if yes, provide IACUC review status and animal welfare assurance information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If YES to vertebrate animals: indicate whether IACUC review is pending or complete, provide IACUC approval date, and include Animal Welfare Assurance Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary/privileged information disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate whether proprietary or privileged information is included in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the appropriate box (Yes/No). NIH will apply FOIA exemptions and may redact confidential commercial/financial information in FOIA responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact and NEPA questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must state whether the project has an actual or potential impact on the environment and, if yes, explain and indicate whether an EA or EIS has been performed or exemption authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanation if any environmental impact exists and documentation about environmental assessment (EA) or environmental impact statement (EIS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic place designation question
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate whether the research performance site is designated, or eligible to be designated, as a historic place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, provide explanation; otherwise check 'No' as in the sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: International activities/collaborations disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate whether the project involves activities outside the United States or partnerships with international collaborators and identify countries if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No and provide country identification and optional explanation for international components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical sketches (biosketches) for Senior/key personnel must follow the prescribed format and DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include NAME, POSITION TITLE, eRA Commons user name, EDUCATION/TRAINING (begin with baccalaureate), and follow the specified order and content headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch content sections (A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: A biosketch should include sections A. Personal Statement, B. Positions and Honors, C. Contributions to Science, and D. Research Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A: Personal Statement describing relevance of applicant's experience to the project; B: Chronological positions and honors; C: Concise contributions to science illustrated by key publications and explanation of significance; D: Ongoing and completed research support, with dates and roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science — include specific examples and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Contributions to Science section, highlight specific areas of contribution with brief explanatory text and representative citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise paragraphs describing major contributions (e.g., structure/function of inteins, chromatin regulation, protein chemistry in living cells, virulence regulation in S. aureus) and list representative publications with citations/PMIDs/PMCID when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current & Pending Support and Other Attachments for key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach Current & Pending Support documents and other required files for PD/PI and senior/key personnel (e.g., biosketch, current & pending support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed filenames (examples in sample) and include role, grant numbers, project titles, dates, and funding sources for ongoing and pending projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe institutional environment and collaborative opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities & Other Resources should document the institutional setting, nearby departments/centers, shared core facilities, and collaborative interactions that will support the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight proximity to relevant departments and resources (e.g., genomics center, proteomics, crystallography, imaging), support staff (glass blower, mechanical workshop, computing support), and administrative infrastructure (electronic purchasing, facility maintenance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document screening/compound libraries and specialized core capabilities when proposing screens
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing target-based or small-molecule screens, describe screening center resources, compound libraries, dispensing technologies, instrumentation, and data analysis pipelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample describes Princeton University Screening Center (PUSC) capabilities: 75,000 singleton compounds, access to 1.4M compound collection, EnVision and Cytation plate readers, Labcyte ECHO 550 acoustic dispenser, Agilent Bravo liquid handler, custom ASMS system with Thermo QExactive orbitrap and CHALIS software, and cheminformatics/visualization tools (Chemaxon InstantJChem, Perkin-Elmer Spotfire).

rubrics_metrics.name: List major equipment and analytical resources with relevance to proposed aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed list of major equipment (mass spectrometers, HPLCs, peptide synthesizers, NMRs, cryoprobes, FPLCs, microscopes, plate readers, centrifuges, ultracentrifuges) and explain how they will be used in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie equipment capabilities to specific assays or aims (e.g., MS/MS analysis of peptides, synthesis of peptides up to 40 amino acids, proteomics analyses, NMR for structural studies). Indicate shared/core equipment availability and staff support.
